A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Scalable In-Context Q-Learning, renamed from SICQL to S-ICQL. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning evaluations, component ablations, dataset-quality experiments and hyperparameter studies in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds out-of-distribution evaluations and training-task comparisons against dataset-best returns in Sections 4.3–4.4.

M1.justification: The frozen world-model prompts, three-head transformer, Bellman/expectile/AWR losses, joint objective and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The renamed S-ICQL and new architecture/optimization subsections explain existing components rather than introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover DarkRoom, Push, Reach, Cheetah-Vel, Walker-Param and Ant-Dir, retaining the same target ranges and Mixed/Medium data types. The added OOD study repartitions existing target ranges, while the stitching study evaluates retained training tasks; these change evaluation design within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The seven main baselines remain. Appendix E changes IC-IQL's stated value update from backbone-plus-head training to head-only training, without establishing that experiments were rerun. The new stitching comparison also introduces dataset-best OPT as a reference alongside DPT and w/o_q.

E3.justification: v2 adds two distinct evaluation designs: training on lower target velocities/directions and testing on higher targets for OOD evaluation, and evaluating suboptimal-data-trained models on their training tasks against dataset-best returns. Existing benchmark budgets and return metrics are retained. Exact OOD partition cutoffs are not specified.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 add OOD robustness tests and a dedicated investigation of whether learned policies exceed dataset-best returns. These substantially extend the analyses beyond v1's component ablations, data-quality tests, hyperparameter sweeps and visualizations, all of which remain after matching appendix relocations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means over 10 evaluation trials, 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals and numerical standard errors. No changed run counts, seed reporting or statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, ablation and hyperparameter table values match. New OOD results include -83.45 ± 2.58 on Cheetah-Vel and 664.95 ± 28.95 on Ant-Dir (v2 Table 3). Figure 4 adds training-task returns of -59.45 and 620.69 versus dataset-best -71.67 and 514.67, respectively. These are additional settings, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The stated expectile domain changes from ω in (0,1) to (0.5,1), narrowing the mathematical specification. However, v2 Table 8 retains ω=0.5 for Push and Reach, creating an inconsistency. No new theorem or proof is added; the prompt reformulation restates existing encodings.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same core claims about combining world-model prompts and dynamic programming for scalable ICRL and effective learning from suboptimal data. The added experiments support those retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains OOD performance through shared environment structure, including kinematics and locomotion, and interprets exceeding dataset-best returns as stitching suboptimal segments into globally optimal policies. These add substantive interpretations. Existing prompt-length limitations and visualization interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.6 newly discloses sampling 200 transitions per task for the retained visualization, and the reproducibility statement says code is provided in supplementary materials. Conversely, Appendix D removes v1's 1,000 DarkRoom trajectories per task. Architecture details, hyperparameter tables, hardware and training-time information otherwise remain.

R1.justification: v2 removes citations to GPT-4, DeepSeek-R1, Nagabandi et al. (2018) and Burda et al. (2019), and revises its architectural contrast with IC-IQL's gradient updates. The principal related-work coverage remains; conversion to author-year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the method exposition into problem statement, architecture, world-model pretraining, Q-learning and overall optimization subsections. It condenses introductory and experimental descriptions, moves hyperparameter discussion to Appendix G, and adds ethics, reproducibility and editorial-LLM statements. Terminology and author information also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds OOD Table 3/Figure 3 and stitching Figure 4, transposes the ablation table, moves ablation curves to Appendix H and hyperparameter tables to Appendix G, and relocates the overview figure. Plot labels change from Average Reward to Average Return, alongside substantial typography and page-layout reformatting.

improvement.justification: The new OOD tests and dataset-best comparisons provide useful evidence for extrapolation and learning beyond collected behavior, while reorganized method exposition improves clarity. The gain is limited by unspecified OOD cutoffs, a globally optimal stitching interpretation stronger than the return comparison establishes, removal of the DarkRoom sample count, and the new expectile-range inconsistency with Table 8.
